svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.20.5.1 Masonry Support
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.20 MASONRY AND INSULATING CONCRETE FORM WALLS NOT IN CONTACT WITH THE GROUND
Masonry Support

g.text: Supporting wall at least as thick

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
All masonry is supported on masonry, concrete
or steel, except that masonry veneer walls may
be supported on foundations of wood frame
built to Sentence 9.15.2.4.(1).
Every masonry wall is at least as thick as the
wall it supports, except as permitted in
Article 9.20.12.2.
Veneer on wood framing
Wood framing is not normally used to carry
masonry veneer because it shrinks. Where it is,
as on a preserved wood foundation, differential
movement is minimized or accommodated, and Part 4
design principles make the support rigid enough
for the masonry.
Sentence 9.15.2.4.(1)
Wood-frame foundations conform to CSA S406 or
Part 4.
Drawn: walls cut through. C is schematic, not a foundation design. Sizes in D are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.20.5.1. (page 9-141)
